books.title: Pride and Prejudice
books.author: Jane Austen
books.description: Elizabeth Bennet spars with the proud Mr. Darcy while her family's future hangs on who marries whom. Sharp, funny, and still the template for a slow-burn love story.

books.title: Dracula
books.author: Bram Stoker
books.description: A solicitor's trip to Transylvania unleashes an ancient count on London. Told entirely through letters, diaries and clippings, which is what makes it so unsettling.

books.title: The Hobbit
books.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
books.description: Bilbo Baggins would rather stay home, but a wizard and thirteen dwarves have other plans. A quest, a dragon, and one very good riddle contest.

books.title: Frankenstein
books.author: Mary Shelley
books.description: A young scientist builds a living creature and then refuses to take responsibility for it. A book about ambition, loneliness and what we owe the things we make.

books.author: George Orwell
books.description: Winston Smith works at rewriting history for a government that watches everything. A bleak, precise warning about surveillance and the control of language.

books.title: Jane Eyre
books.author: Charlotte Brontë
books.description: An orphan becomes a governess at Thornfield Hall and finds a secret in the attic. Gothic atmosphere, a stubborn heroine, and a very unusual proposal.

books.title: The Great Gatsby
books.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
books.description: Nick Carraway watches his mysterious neighbour throw lavish parties in the hope of winning back one woman. A short, glittering book about wanting the past back.

books.title: Dune
books.author: Frank Herbert
books.description: Paul Atreides inherits a desert planet that is the only source of the most valuable substance in the universe. Politics, ecology and prophecy on a huge scale.

books.title: Little Women
books.author: Louisa May Alcott
books.description: Four sisters grow up in New England during the Civil War. Jo March wants to be a writer, and the book knows exactly how much that costs her.

books.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
books.author: Oscar Wilde
books.description: A beautiful young man stays unchanged while his portrait absorbs every consequence of his choices. Witty on the surface, genuinely dark underneath.

books.title: The Time Machine
books.author: H.G. Wells
books.description: An inventor travels to the year 802,701 and finds humanity split into two very different species. A quick read with a long shadow.

books.title: Emma
books.author: Jane Austen
books.description: Emma Woodhouse is sure she is an excellent matchmaker, and is wrong about almost everyone, including herself. Austen's most playful heroine.

books.title: A Study in Scarlet
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: The first meeting of Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson, and the first case they solve together. A body, a single word written in blood, and a long flashback.

books.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: A family curse, a phantom dog on the moor, and Holmes working out which of those is real. The best atmosphere of any Holmes story.

books.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
books.author: Lewis Carroll
books.description: Alice follows a white rabbit down a hole into a world where the rules of logic have been quietly removed. Funnier and stranger than its reputation.

books.title: Wuthering Heights
books.author: Emily Brontë
books.description: Heathcliff and Catherine's doomed attachment on the Yorkshire moors, told by two unreliable narrators. Nobody in it is likeable, which is the point.

books.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: Twelve short cases, including "A Scandal in Bohemia" and "The Speckled Band". The easiest way into the detective genre, and still one of the best.

books.title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
books.author: C.S. Lewis
books.description: Four siblings step through a wardrobe into a land stuck in endless winter. A children's book that adults keep returning to.

userBooks.review: Every re-read finds a new joke. The first proposal scene is perfect.
Cosy and adventurous in equal measure. The riddle chapter is the best part.
The epistolary format makes the dread build slowly. Renfield steals every scene.
Beautifully written, but I never warmed to anyone in it.
Could not get past the second narrator. Might try again in winter.

profile.bio: Reads classics in the evening and sci-fi on the weekend. Always one book behind on the reading goal.
